cases.why: the step that proves every rule can fail is replaced by a no-op. The job still goes green on a real page -- which is exactly what it would do if a rule had gone blind, so green stops meaning anything.
the real check runs without --axe, so the axe rule is skipped on the page while the self-test still proves axe works on its fixture -- a green job with no accessibility scan in it.
Playwright floats to whatever is newest, so a browser update can change what 'no findings' means on a day nobody changed anything.
a pull request that changes only the self-hosted font no longer runs the checks, though a changed font is a changed page -- the font check is the one most likely to catch it.
the checker runs two widths instead of six, and the 360px phone -- where the reliability points were smallest -- is not one of them.
the network-allowed pass goes, so the layout with ESPN's logos actually loaded is never checked -- and a loaded logo is what changes the card's size.
the target floor drops to 20px, which quietly passes the 21-22px reliability points this check was built to catch.
the font rule's fixture is renamed, so the self-test no longer proves the font rule can fail while still printing 'every rule caught its fixture'.

the font rule leans on document.fonts.check(), which answers true when nothing is pending -- including when no face was ever declared. CLAUDE.md records it gating three measurement scripts that proved nothing.
cases.find:
await document.fonts.ready;
  await document.fonts.load("700 16px 'Plus Jakarta Sans'");

cases.why: the fitting table header goes back to top:0 below 1080px, under the sticky top bar -- the Stage 30 item 2 defect, which nothing but a render showed for as long as it shipped.

the bar's height is read once at load and never again, so when the title wraps or the safe area changes the headers stick a few pixels under the bar -- a partial return of the defect on exactly the phones least likely to be tested.
the sticky rule's fixture is renamed, so the self-test no longer proves the rule can fail while still printing 'every rule caught its fixture'.
the sticky rule stops asking what is drawn and trusts the header itself. The header's rectangle was exactly where it belonged the whole time the bar covered it, so this version passes the defect.

cases.why: the rule is defined and has a fixture, and is never run on the real page: the self-test goes on passing while the page check checks nothing.
